The closest match is Mathur et al.’s “Retrieval Improvements Do Not Guarantee Better Answers: A Study of RAG for AI Policy QA,” which studies RAG for AI governance and policy analysis using the AGORA corpus and finds that better retrieval does not consistently improve end-to-end QA [1]. It specifically reports that domain-specific fine-tuning improves retrieval metrics but can still fail to improve answer quality, and may even increase confident hallucinations when relevant documents are missing [1].

If you meant a broader RAG-for-policy search, this set is otherwise mostly about medical, industrial, financial, multimodal, or general QA rather than policy QA [2-10].
